newsitem.title: USA: Hughes Electronics earnings fall in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Hughes Electronics earnings fall in quarter.

text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp., whose defence operations are being sold to Raytheon Co., Monday said earnings fell 5 percent in the fourth quarter, hurt by auto workers' strikes last year in the United States and Canada.

Hughes, a unit of General Motors Corp. that makes electronic parts for autos and aircraft, telecommunications equipment, satellites and defence products, said net earnings fell to $250.3 million, or 70 cents a share, from $263.9 million, or 74 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Revenues rose 7 percent to $4.30 billion from $4.03 billion.
GM agreed on Jan. 16 to sell Hughes' aircraft and defence operations to Lexington, Mass.-based Raytheon in a $9.5 billion deal that will create the nation's third-biggest defence contractor.
GM is retaining Hughes' lucrative telecommunications and space unit, which builds satellites and operates the fast-growing DirecTV satellite broadcasting service.
GM got hit by strikes in Canada, as well as Indiana and Wisconsin, last October and November that hurt vehicle production and curtailed Hughes' sales of radios and other electronic components.

Los Angeles-based Hughes said operating earnings in its automotive electronics business fell 57 percent in the quarter as revenues fell 11 percent to $1.25 billion. It cited a 12 percent drop in GM vehicle production and said its electronic content fell 1 percent to $902 per GM vehicle in the quarter.

Profits in Hughes' telecommunications and space business jumped 44 percent as revenues rose 31 percent to $1.22 billion. The gain came from strength in Hughes' DirecTV satellite TV business and higher sales of cellular communications gear and commercial satellites, Hughes said.
Operating profit in aerospace and defence rose 8 percent as revenues grew 11 percent to $1.79 billion.
Hughes stock rose 50 cents to $61.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
